scale.source: CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) ro %spellout-cardinal-masculine: "1000000000: <%spellout-cardinal-neuter< miliard;", "1000000000000: <%spellout-cardinal-neuter< bilion;": Romanian counts in the long scale.; DEX '09, "bilion": "Număr egal cu o mie de miliarde sau (în unele țări) cu un miliard."; the first sense, 10^12, is the long scale.

group_mark.source: CLDR 48 ro number symbols (ICU 78 formats 1234567.5 as "1.234.567,5"): the dot groups digits.

decimal_mark.source: CLDR 48 ro number symbols (ICU 78 formats 1234567.5 as "1.234.567,5"): the comma marks the decimals.

space_groups.source: CLDR 48 ro number symbols group digits with a dot, so a space separates two numbers.

plural_scale_needs_count.source: "milioane de oameni" names no number; "două milioane" does.

scale_noun_agrees.source: A scale noun agrees in number with its count. DOOM 3: "milion2 (un ~) [...] num.; 1.000.000", "milioane (două/trei etc. ~)"; "mie1 (o ~)", "mie2 s. f. [...] pl. mii".

joiner_tens_units.source: CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) ro %spellout-cardinal-masculine: "21: <%spellout-cardinal-feminine<zeci și >%spellout-cardinal-masculine>;": "și" joins the tens and the units.

joiner_after_hundred.source: CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) ro %spellout-cardinal-masculine: "201: <%spellout-cardinal-feminine< sute >%spellout-cardinal-masculine>;": no joiner after the hundreds.

joiner_between_groups.source: CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) ro %spellout-cardinal-masculine: "2001: <%spellout-cardinal-feminine< mii >%spellout-cardinal-masculine>;"; "o mie și una de nopți" keeps "și" in a set phrase; reading accepts both.

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) ro %spellout-cardinal-masculine: "2001: <%spellout-cardinal-feminine< mii >%spellout-cardinal-masculine>;": no joiner after the thousands; "și" stays only in the set phrase "o mie și una de nopți", before a group below a hundred.

small_multiplier_starts_group.source: unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 (CLDR RBNF ro data), %spellout-cardinal, rendering of 1100 and 2100: "o mie o sută", "două mii o sută": the hundred after the thousands is the next group, so a hundred multiplier counts no group of thousands.

comma_between_classes.source: The CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) ro rules quoted for joiner_between_groups write no comma between two classes. No source opened shows a comma between two classes of one number, so a comma ends a number.

joiner_before_last_group.source: CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) ro %spellout-cardinal-masculine: "2001: <%spellout-cardinal-feminine< mii >%spellout-cardinal-masculine>;": no joiner before the last group; "o mie și una de nopți" keeps "și" in a set phrase. Reading accepts both.

ordinal_style.source: Wikipedia (ro), "Numeral": "al o sută douăzeci și unulea (stâlp), a o sută douăzeci și una (cerere)": only the last word takes the ordinal ending.

letter_folds.source: Wikipedia (ro), "Ș": "în anul 2003 un consiliu științific al Institutului de Lingvistică al Academiei Române a stabilit că semnul corect este virgula, nu sedila"; older text uses the cedilla letters, so "ş" and "ţ" read as "ș" and "ț".

decimal_marker.source: CLDR 48 RBNF (ICU 78) ro %spellout-cardinal-masculine: "x.x: <%spellout-cardinal-masculine< virgulă >%spellout-cardinal-masculine>;"; "virgula" is the same word without diacritics. DEX '09, "virgulă": "Semn întrebuințat pentru a separa, într-un număr zecimal, partea întreagă de partea fracționară."

minus_idioms.source: No Romanian idiom puts "minus" before a positive number.

article_one.source: "un" and "o" are also the indefinite article; alone before a noun they are a weak number ("am o casă").

of.source: "un milion de oameni": "de" after a scale noun; a plural collective after it multiplies the count.

fraction_of.source: "o treime de kilogram": "de" goes on to the noun; the list has no collective noun for a fraction to multiply.

denominator_particle.source: Romanian has no particle like pt "avos".

class_noun.source: No Romanian class noun is read.

half_unit.source: "și jumătate" follows the noun in Romanian ("un kilogram și jumătate").

lone_decimal_mark.source: Structural, no external source: a group mark stands only between digits, so a point right before the first digit marks decimals, as in pt-PT: ".5" is 0.5. CLDR 48 ro number symbols: decimal ",", so ",5" is 0.5.

range_cue.source: DEX '09, "între": "6. (Indică o aproximare) Să vii între 12 și 13."

count_of.source: Wikipedia, "Romanian numbers", Preposition de: "The preposition de is also used within the syntax of the number itself, for stating the number of thousands, millions, billions, etc.: douăzeci de mii [...] it is used when the last two digits of the number of thousands, millions, etc. are 00 or 20–99." DOOM 3 shows it in "o ~ de dolari"; no national source states the rule as a sentence. Reading also accepts "de" after any count.
